_comment: Placeholder content overlay. The real copy lives in content.local.json (git-ignored). cameras lists the camera words: prefix is how the prompt scraper cases the same word when a provider names it. A local overlay has to carry this key: a placeholder prefix standing in for a real one would be written into the library's sidecars. Fun Time's overlay lists the same words under its own cameras key, as the words its players set apart from the act on a row, so the two must agree. chrome_profile and scrape_provider are the machine-specific values the app needs at runtime. Where the library is, where the apps' checkouts are, Genau's flick words, the 0_inbox folder a Genau flick arrives in, and the folders Genau, Origenerator and Warm Gun keep in the library are not here: they are the settings all of Haglio shares, written once in ~/.haglio/settings.json (app_support.haglio_settings). retired_root is optional too: where a non-AI original goes once its upscale is made, with its sidecar and funscript beside it. Omit it and the original stays in the library, in its bucket's '2*' folder, which is what the user does by hand; set it to somewhere off the working drive when those folders would otherwise fill it. excerpt_folders is optional: library-relative folders holding scenes carved out of longer videos and nothing else, for the batches that were split before anything recorded a clip block; it is here rather than in source because a folder name is library vocabulary. topaz_ffmpeg and topaz_models are optional: where Topaz Video's own ffmpeg build and its models are, for a machine whose installer put them somewhere other than Program Files and ProgramData. Both upscale stages drive that build and no other, so a wrong path stops the pipeline at its dependency check. version_overrides is optional: stem -> the stem of the video it is a version of, for the version families neither the naming rule nor the frames can settle (a trim saved under a new name, say), both in one bucket. It is here rather than in source because both halves of a pair are library filenames. display_timezone is optional: the zone a run's timestamps are shown in, e.g. America/Los_Angeles; omit it and they are shown in whatever zone the machine says it is in. warm_gun_outbox names the folder outside the library that Warm Gun still writes its journal to, read alongside the library's own copy; omit it once the app writes into the library. vr_videos is optional: where the library's VR folder is kept when it is not on the library's own drive, a cloud drive say. Their funscripts stay in the library's scripts tree under VR, and the scripts stage matches a script against them as though they sat in the library; omit it and the VR videos are looked for in the library itself.
